fields.footer_copy: An informational platform focused on trade between African and European markets.

fields.hero_detail: EuroAfrica provides a clear view of the key commodities and manufactured goods moving between Africa and Europe. From agricultural produce and strategic minerals to machinery, pharmaceuticals and transport equipment, explore the sectors driving commercial exchange across both continents.
fields.final_heading: Discover the Trade Connecting Africa and Europe
fields.final_text: Explore key industries, understand important product categories and discover the commercial connections between African and European markets.
fields.hero_heading: Connecting Africa and Europe Through Trade
fields.hero_text: Discover the products, industries and opportunities shaping trade between two dynamic markets.
fields.hero_alt: Aerial view of a container ship at sea
fields.hero_caption: Illustrative photograph by Bent Van Aeken / Unsplash.
fields.direction_heading: Two Continents. Diverse Markets. Growing Opportunities.
fields.direction_text:
Africa and Europe are connected by established trade relationships spanning agriculture, manufacturing, energy, infrastructure and consumer goods.

African markets supply Europe with valuable agricultural commodities, horticultural produce, minerals and manufactured goods, while European industries provide African markets with machinery, transport equipment, pharmaceuticals, refined products and foodstuffs.

EuroAfrica brings these trade flows together in one accessible platform, helping businesses, professionals and interested stakeholders understand what is traded, where key products originate and the sectors creating commercial opportunities between the two regions.
fields.about_heading: Understand the Trade Behind the Markets
fields.about_text: International trade can be complex. EuroAfrica makes the landscape easier to understand by organising key trade categories, products and market information into a clear and accessible resource.
fields.diversity_heading: Explore a Trade Relationship Built on Complementary Strengths
fields.diversity_text:
Africa and Europe bring different strengths to international trade.

Africa combines agricultural capacity, natural resources and expanding manufacturing industries. Europe contributes advanced machinery, transportation systems, pharmaceuticals, industrial products and established manufacturing capabilities.

Together, these complementary strengths create trade relationships across numerous sectors and markets.

EuroAfrica helps you explore those connections and identify the categories shaping commerce between the two continents.
fields.diversity_alt: Woven baskets and hats on a textured surface
fields.diversity_caption: Illustrative photograph by Anes mchayaa / Unsplash.
fields.contact_text:
Whether you're researching a particular product category, exploring a market or looking for information about trade between Africa and Europe, you can contact us with your enquiry.

Tell us what you're interested in and provide the relevant details. Our team will review your enquiry and respond using the contact information provided.

fields.summary: European exports to Africa span industrial equipment, transportation, healthcare, energy and food.

fields.heading: European Products Supporting African Markets
fields.introduction: These products serve businesses, governments, industries and consumers across African markets while supporting infrastructure development, manufacturing and everyday economic activity.

fields.title: Agricultural Commodities
fields.summary: From African farms to international markets.
fields.image_alt: Roasted coffee beans in processing equipment
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Alex Jones / Unsplash.
fields.overview:
Africa is an important source of globally traded agricultural commodities. Cocoa from Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana, coffee from Ethiopia and Kenya, and sesame seeds from countries including Ethiopia, Sudan and Tanzania represent some of the continent's established agricultural exports.

These commodities connect African producers and supply chains with food, beverage and processing industries across international markets.

Product form is an important distinction: whole beans, seeds and processed ingredients have different uses in food and beverage production. A useful category enquiry identifies the commodity, intended application and destination market, leaving grade, packaging and traceability details to be confirmed for the specific product.

fields.title: Horticulture
fields.summary: Fresh produce cultivated for demanding international markets.
fields.image_alt: Sliced avocado on a green surface
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Louis Hansel / Unsplash.
fields.overview:
Africa's varied climates and agricultural regions support the production of fresh fruits, vegetables, avocados and flowers for export.

Countries including Kenya, Morocco and Zimbabwe contribute to horticultural trade, supplying products ranging from fresh produce to cut roses.

Fruit, vegetables and cut flowers require different handling, presentation and timing. Variety, maturity and intended use help distinguish one item from another. For a focused enquiry, name the crop and planned use, and identify any storage or delivery considerations that need product-specific confirmation.

fields.title: Raw Minerals & Metals
fields.summary: Resources supporting global industry and technology.
fields.overview:
Africa holds significant reserves of minerals and metals used across manufacturing, infrastructure, energy and technology industries.

Copper and cobalt from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Zambia, alongside gold and platinum from South Africa and other producing regions, form part of the continent's important mineral trade.

Mineral-bearing material, concentrates and refined metals should not be treated as interchangeable products. Their composition and processing stage affect their industrial use. Clear product identification and independently verified analysis are important when interpreting a category description; this overview does not establish a grade or a particular source.

fields.title: Textiles & Apparel
fields.image_alt: Woven baskets and hats on a textured surface
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Anes mchayaa / Unsplash.
fields.overview:
Africa's textile, clothing and footwear industries contribute to trade with European markets, supported in some cases by preferential trade arrangements such as Economic Partnership Agreements.

The sector represents an important intersection between local manufacturing, employment, international supply chains and access to overseas markets.

Fabrics, finished garments and footwear serve different users and applications. Fibre composition, construction, sizing and care requirements provide a practical basis for comparing items. Product-specific discussions should distinguish materials and intended use without assuming a particular brand, certification or manufacturing capacity.

fields.title: Machinery & Appliances
fields.summary: Over €41 billion in machinery and appliances supporting industry, production and infrastructure.
fields.image_alt: Industrial machinery with pipes and valves
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Dave Meckler / Unsplash.
fields.overview:
Valued at more than €41 billion, machinery and appliances represent the largest export category from Europe to Africa. The sector includes industrial factory equipment, power generators and specialised machinery supporting manufacturing, infrastructure development and productive industries across African markets.

Equipment should be considered in the context of the process it is intended to support. Operating conditions, power compatibility, maintenance access and integration with existing equipment can matter as much as the machine type. A detailed enquiry should describe the application and the information needed to assess suitability, rather than assume a standard configuration.

fields.title: Transport Equipment
fields.image_alt: Vehicle lights organized in storage bins
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Diego Romeo / Unsplash.
fields.overview:
European transport exports to African markets include passenger vehicles, heavy-duty trucks, commercial aircraft, railway equipment and related transportation technologies.

These products support passenger mobility, logistics, construction, public transportation and commercial supply chains across the continent.

Complete vehicles, replacement components and specialist transport systems need different kinds of identification. Intended duty, compatibility and supporting documentation help clarify what is being discussed. For parts or equipment, a precise reference and operating context are more useful than a broad category name; availability and service arrangements require separate confirmation.

fields.title: Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Volodymyr Hryshchenko / Unsplash.
fields.overview:
European chemical and pharmaceutical exports serve a wide range of African sectors.

Products include pharmaceuticals and medical supplies as well as industrial chemicals and synthetic fertilisers used by healthcare providers, agricultural operations and industrial businesses.

Medicinal products, industrial substances and agricultural inputs must be distinguished by their intended use. Names alone do not establish composition, safe handling or suitability for a market. Product documentation and the applicable professional review are essential to a specific assessment; this page provides category information, not medical or application advice.

fields.title: Refined Mineral Products & Fuels
fields.summary: Energy products serving markets with diverse refining capacities.
fields.image_alt: Distillation structures at a refinery at dusk
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Anthony Maw / Unsplash.
fields.overview:
Refined petroleum products and fuels form another component of Europe-to-Africa trade, particularly in markets where domestic refining capacity does not fully meet demand.

These products support transportation, industry, commercial activity and broader energy requirements.

Finished fuels, lubricating products and other refined materials differ in composition and application. A category name should not be read as a specification. Identifying the material and intended use provides a starting point for reviewing relevant documentation, handling requirements and compatibility without assuming that products are interchangeable.

fields.title: Agri-food & Foodstuffs
fields.summary: Food products connecting European producers with African consumers.
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Ann Savchenko / Unsplash.
fields.overview:
European agricultural and food exports include wheat, dairy products and a broad range of processed consumer foods.

These goods form part of established food supply chains serving retail, hospitality, food processing and consumer markets across Africa.

Bulk ingredients and packaged foods have different presentation, storage and labelling needs. Ingredient composition, allergens and the intended retail or processing use help define an enquiry. The relevant product information should be checked individually; this overview does not establish shelf life, dietary certification or the availability of any particular brand.

fields.title: Tobacco Products
fields.summary: A regulated category within international trade.
fields.overview:
Tobacco products are also traded from European producers into certain African markets. As a regulated product category, their importation, distribution and sale are subject to the applicable laws, duties and public-health requirements of individual markets.

Category-level trade information should be read separately from product-specific claims. Packaging descriptions and catalogue entries do not establish market approval, availability or authorization. This page offers a neutral overview of the category; requirements and public-health information must be checked with the relevant authorities for the market concerned.

fields.title: About EuroAfrica
fields.summary: EuroAfrica is an informational platform focused on trade between African and European markets.
fields.image_alt: Aerial view of a container ship at sea
fields.image_caption: Illustrative photograph by Bent Van Aeken / Unsplash.
fields.body:
Our purpose is to make key trade categories and market connections easier to discover and understand. We present information across sectors including agriculture, horticulture, minerals, textiles, machinery, transportation, pharmaceuticals, energy products and food.

By bringing these categories together in a structured and accessible format, EuroAfrica provides a starting point for businesses, professionals, researchers and other stakeholders interested in understanding the commercial links between Africa and Europe.

fields.heading: Our Focus
fields.text:
We focus on presenting trade information clearly, professionally and responsibly.

Rather than overwhelming visitors with unnecessary complexity, EuroAfrica highlights the products, sectors and markets that contribute to trade between the two regions.

fields.heading: Our Vision
fields.text: To become a trusted and accessible source of information for understanding the products, industries and opportunities connecting African and European markets.
